newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - SUPER BOWL PRACTICES DAMPENED BY RAIN.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - SUPER BOWL PRACTICES DAMPENED BY RAIN.

text.p: Rain on Friday forced the Green Bay Packers to curtail practice for the Super Bowl but the New England Patriots had a full workout.
While weather will not be a factor in Sunday's Super Bowl XXXI inside the Louisiana Superdome, heavy rain prevented the Packers from getting in their last full practice.
"Actually it may work out for the best because they are happy about it," Packers coach Mike Holmgren said after he sent his players back to their hotel after only 10 minutes of work.
"We could have gone through a walk-through, but the field was pretty slippery and I didn't want anyone to pull a muscle at this stage."
Holmgren decided to end the morning practice session when he saw tight end Mark Chmura slip while trying to turn on the team's outdoor practice field.
The Patriots, meanwhile, managed to get in a full 75-minute workout later when there was a break in the weather, although the field's artificial surface was still wet.
The players did not wear their full uniforms -- just helmets, shorts and T-shirts.
"I can't ask any more of our guys from a preparation standpoint," New England coach Bill Parcells said. "They're ready to play the game now."
